preamble: Centralization and raising of the mid back rounded vowel [o] to the close-mid central rounded [ɵ]. In Russian, stressed /o/ after a palatalized (soft) consonant is centralized and raised to [ɵ], as in тётя [ˈtʲɵtʲə] 'aunt' and нёс [nʲʷɵs] '(he) carried', while after hard consonants it stays back (бок [bˠʷok] 'side'); Wikipedia gives the rule after Jones & Ward (1969) and Halle (1959). Yanushevskaya & Bunčić (2015) describe the same fronting of Russian vowels after, and most strongly between, palatalized consonants, but transcribe /o/ in that position as advanced [o̟], as in Stëpin [ˈstʲo̟ˑpʲɪn] 'of Stëpa' (some diacritics omitted). This /o/, spelled ё, developed from stressed e, as in тёплый /ˈtʲopɫij/ 'warm' beside тепло /tʲiˈpɫo/ 'heat' (e → o). Stressed /u/ is centralized to [ʉ] between soft consonants in the same way (u → ʉ).

examples.note: The soft consonant is also labialized before the rounded vowel. After a hard consonant /o/ stays back: бок [bˠʷok] 'side'.
In село the stressed /o/ follows hard /ɫ/ and stays [o].

sources: Yanushevskaya, I., & Bunčić, D. (2015). Russian. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 45(2), 221–228. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100314000395
